questions.subject: Heaps
questions.question: What is heap sort in Heaps and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: heap sort in Heaps refers to in-place comparison sort. It works by O(n log n) worst case, O(1) space. Key characteristics include build max heap, repeatedly extract max. Example: buildHeap(arr); for (int i = n-1; i > 0; i--) { swap(arr[0], arr[i]); heapify(arr, i, 0); }. Common pitfalls include unstable sort, cache inefficiency.

questions.subject: Heaps
questions.question: Explain the difference between build heap and extract max in Heaps.
questions.ideal_answer: build heap and extract max differ in several ways: build heap is heap construction from array (works by O(n) optimal bottom-up) whereas extract max is removing root element (works by replace root with last, heapify root). build heap is typically used for heapify from last non-leaf to root, while extract max is used for O(log n) operation. Example demonstrating build heap: for (int i = n/2 - 1; i >= 0; i--) heapify(arr, n, i);. Example demonstrating extract max: int max = arr[0]; arr[0] = arr[n-1]; heapify(arr, n-1, 0);.

questions.subject: Heaps
questions.question: Explain the difference between heap property and array representation in Heaps.
questions.ideal_answer: heap property and array representation differ in several ways: heap property is parent-child ordering (works by max-heap: parent >= children; min-heap: parent <= children) whereas array representation is implicit complete tree storage (works by no pointer overhead). heap property is typically used for not a sorted structure, partial order, while array representation is used for parent i -> children 2i+1, 2i+2; child i -> parent (i-1)/2. Example demonstrating heap property: arr[i] >= arr[2*i+1] && arr[i] >= arr[2*i+2]. Example demonstrating array representation: int[] heap = new int[n];.

questions.question: What is heapify in Heaps and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: heapify in Heaps refers to maintaining heap property. It works by O(log n) sift down. Key characteristics include compare with children, swap with larger (max-heap), recurse. Example: void heapify(int[] arr, int n, int i) { int largest = i; int l = 2*i+1; int r = 2*i+2; if (l < n && arr[l] > arr[largest]) largest = l; ... }. Common pitfalls include bottom-up build heap O(n).

questions.question: What is median from stream in Heaps and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: median from stream in Heaps refers to running median calculation. It works by dual heap: max-heap lower, min-heap upper. Key characteristics include rebalance heaps to size difference <= 1. Example: maxHeap.offer(num); minHeap.offer(maxHeap.poll()); if (maxHeap.size() < minHeap.size()) maxHeap.offer(minHeap.poll());. Common pitfalls include median = maxHeap.peek() or average.
